questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking, different courses, a city unexplored

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was hard since no one else from KU were going (at least not that I know of) so I had no connection to other danish students, which made the adjustment period longer than anticipated, but it also means that I've been 'forced' to make irish friends for which im deeply appreciative

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: TCD helps you a lot bur you have to ask

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: the academic registry was helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was terrible, and very. very expensive. I lived in student accommodation (I got very lucky), and it was 1250€ a month for 12 m2 w. own bathroom, share kitchen and living room facilities. Great area Stoney batter but shite bed, Molly bathroom unaccommodating staff. But its only 4 months so you manage.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Area is crucial, the prices are off the roof. Start very early to avoid stress and multiple moving during semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was super easy, you can change your courses during the first couple of weeks, meaning you can attend the first lecture and see if its for you or not. SO don't stress about the courses submitted prior to departure.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get emails about everything and the orientation is helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again Academic registry is an office where you can get help if something is not working out with your courses or registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very successful, I registered for updated courses upon arrival, I changed 2 of them after realising they weren't for me, and It turned out perfect.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress, just follow the instructions via email and on myTcd you'll be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was Wonderfull super interesting courses and the lectures are genuinely interested and invested in your progress.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: since many of the courses I took were theme-related e.g. race ethnicity and identity, they were different fro, what im used to at UCPH, so it was challenging because it was new, I think the level was suitable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At TCD we have lectures and tutorials. Same amount of classes as in UCPH, but lectures of 50 minutes and following tutorials of 50 minutes, it requires more reading and more preparation but you also learn quite bit more that way because of the expectations of you.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Researching society 
Race ethnicity and identity
Comparative sociology og europe 
Social networks and digital lives
Globalisation and development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Social networks and digital lives was incredible its a senior sophistry module (4th year - as sociology BA Is 4 years at TCD).
Researching society is great quantitative brush up course using state.
Race ethnicity and identity is a very insightful course, its should be compulsory

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Student accommodation often required 'investment' as move in such as a mattress topper, sheets, duvet, pillows, pots, pans, plates, glasses, utensils etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport Is insanely cheep like 75% cheaper than copenhagen.
Eating and drinking out is more or less the same as In CPH. 4-7€ for a pint.
Books are all online or can be borrowed from the TCD library
Tobacco is more expensive 14€ for a pack of straights

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have so many societies like food and drink, fashion, arts, knitting, philosophy, as well as sports like surfing or fencing. Small fees for membership and loads of social events to attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fashion society was great. The surfing trip (michaelmas term) is legendary as well as the ski trip (Hilary term).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I wish I would've seen more cities outside of Dublin like Galway, I recommend going to Howth its only 45 minute ride. Go to many clubs, go out a lot. Be prepared for shite food. Go to butlers for hot chocolate. Go to Book of kells at TCD. Go to the Berkeley library to study. If you smoke learn to roll.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was hard in the beginning of course. It was worth it though in the end.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Irish folks are super nice and very welcoming, but YOU have to approach them. Compliment what they are wearing they love that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Just that I didn't have any danish folks to stick to like so many other reopens did. It made it harder in the beginning. I didn't truly adjust till 2 months in - just be aware that the adjustment can be hard, and don't beat yourself down because of it. just keep trying, show up alone if that's what it takes. Your only there for 4 months so who cares if you make stupid mistakes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pubs

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont stress when info is not available till after you've arrived. 
Look for accommodation early.
Be stylish - TCD students have amazing and personal style

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: just don't stres if you don't fit in immediately

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making Irish friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Felling lonely for the first while
